updates.name: Michelle A. Baker
updates.bio: Professor of Biology at Utah State University who studies how water moving through landscapes shapes ecosystem structure and function, combining ecology, hydrology and geochemistry to examine watershed hydrologic connections, energy flow and nutrient cycling. She earned her PhD at the University of New Mexico working on groundwater organic carbon cycling.
updates.research_interests: hydrologic linkages within watersheds; effects of water movement on ecosystem structure and function; nutrient cycling and energy flow in streams and groundwater; biogeochemistry; ecosystem ecology
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biology, Utah State University
updates.notes: Verified: USU Biology profile 200 (name, Professor, research statement, PhD UNM 1998, dissertation 'Organic Carbon Cycling in Groundwater'). ORCID 0000-0002-7188-8639 record name 'Michelle Baker', employment Utah State University Biology Professor 1999-present; existing ORCID consistent.

updates.name: Molly O. Baringer
updates.bio: Sea-going physical oceanographer at NOAA's Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory in Miami, where she has held deputy and acting director roles. Her Atlantic-focused research covers Florida Current and western boundary current transport, North Atlantic overturning circulation monitoring, XBT observations and repeat hydrography. PhD from the MIT-WHOI Joint Program.
updates.research_interests: meso- to large-scale ocean circulation and the global meridional overturning circulation; Florida Current / western boundary current transport; North Atlantic MOC monitoring (RAPID/MOCHA); high-density XBT observations; repeat hydrography and coastal carbon dioxide surveys
updates.current_affiliation: NOAA Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory (AOML)

updates.name: Monica G. Turner
updates.bio: Professor of Biology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison who leads a mainly terrestrial landscape and ecosystem ecology group that also studies land-water interactions. Using field studies, experiments, spatial analysis and simulation, her lab examines how and why ecosystems change, including shifting fire regimes in Greater Yellowstone forests and climate change effects.
updates.research_interests: landscape ecology (spatial pattern and ecological process); ecosystem ecology; land-water interactions; changing fire regimes and short-interval reburns in Greater Yellowstone forests; climate-change effects on landscapes; simulation modeling
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biology, University of Wisconsin-Madison

He served as 2011 president of the American Society of Agronomy and now runs a consultancy.

His evo-devo work covers body patterning and segmentation, germline regeneration and structural color. National Academy of Sciences member.
